2 MVC No.5140/2021  SCCH-25  JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this Petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ for the Death of one Sriramaiah A.B. in a road traffic accident dated 28.09.2021.

Kamalamma G.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164163181/
1 2.

The case of the Petitioners' in brief is that:
On 28.09.2021 at about 1.50 pm the deceased Sriramaiah A.B. was a pedestrian walking on the extreme left side on Shidlaghatta - Vijayapura Road, near Ramanjinappa House, Meluru Village, Shidlaghatta Taluk, Chikkaballapura.

At that time suddenly the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA40F899 came from opposite direction i.e., from Vijayapura side in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the deceased.
Due to impact the deceased fell down and the wheels of the said bus ran on the body of the deceased.
Consequently the deceased SCCH-25 sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to the fatal injuries and died on the spot.

3. The petitioners further averred that, immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Shidlaghatta Govt. Hospital wherein post mortem examination was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they performed funeral and obsequies ceremonies, by spending more than Rs.1,00,000/.
Due to the sudden and sad demise of the deceased in the tragic accident, the petitioners are undergoing deep mental shock, pain and sufferings.

4. The petitioners further stated that, prior to the date of accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was earning his livelihood as an Agriculturist, earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month and contributing his entire income for welfare and maintenance of his family.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners life has become dark, SCCH-25 miserable and depressed and they are put to great financial hardship.
5. The Shidlaghatta Rural Police have registered a case against the driver of the KSRTC bus in Cr.No.305/2021 p/u/Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC.
The respondent being the RC owner of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA40F899 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
6. In response to the service of notice, the Respondent appeared and filed written statement.

7. The objections of the respondent:
It has stated that, at the time of the alleged accident the driver of the Respondent bus was very moderate in speed and was taking all Road safety measures.
There is no negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC bus.
Further contended that the deceased himself is responsible for the said accident.
The concerned police have registered a false case against the KSRTC driver on the wrong notion that SCCH-25 always heavy vehicles are at wrong and pedestrian are right.

It has denied the age,
income, avocation, dependency of the petitioners and the accident.
It has contended that, compensation claimed by the petitioners is not based on any cogent and reasonable grounds and is imaginary and speculative.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

2 8.

On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sriramaiah A.B.?
2.

Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sriramaiah A.B., died on account of Road Traffic Accident took place on Shidlaghatta - Vijayapura Road, near Ramanjinappa House, Malluru Village, Shidlaghatta Taluk,
Chickkaballapura, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA40F899, dated 28.09.2021 at about 1.50pm?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom payable 4.
What Order or Award?
SCCH-25 9.
In order to prove their case, the Petitioners have examined Petitioner No.1 - Smt.Kamalamma G.R. - Wife of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked 9 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.9.
They have also examined Mr. Pramod - eye witness as PW.2 and produced 1 document as per Ex.P.10.
On the other side, the Respondent examined its Driver Sri.C.V.Muthurayappa as RW.1 but did not produce any documents on his behalf.
10. Heard both the Counsels and perused the materials on record.

11. My finding to the above issues are as follows: Issue Nos.1 & 2 : In the affirmative Issue No.3 : In the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order for the Following:
REASONS 12. Issue No.1:
It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the wife, Petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased - SCCH-25 Sriramaiah A.B.
The Petitioners to prove their relationship have examined the 1st Petitioner as PW.1.
PW.1 has specifically spoken about this relationship in her chief examination.
Apart from that, to prove the relationship, the Petitioners have produced their Notarized copy of Aadhar Cards as per Exs.P.8.
In Ex.P.8 - Aadhar Cards of the petitioner Nos.1 & 2 (wife and son) their husband's and father's name is mentioned as Sriramaiah A.B respectively.
These documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law.
These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondent.

The Respondents have not produced any Kamalamma G.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164163181/
3 contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and the documents, this court is of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 is the Wife and Petitioner No.2 is the son of SCCH-25 the deceased.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

13. Issue No.2:
The Petitioners to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus have examined Petitioner No.1 as PW.1 and produced documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.7.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in her affidavit filed in lieu of her chief examination.

On the other side,
the Respondent has denied the involvement and negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It has contended that, the accident is caused due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased himself.

14. The documents produced by the Petitioners such as the FIR in Cr.No.305/2021 of Shidlaghatta Rural Police, FIS, MVA report, PM report, Inquest Mahazar, spot sketch and charge sheet as per Exs.P.1 to P.7 are all public documents and have initial presumptive value under law.
SCCH-25
These documents fully and completely corroborate with the evidence of PW.1.

The investigation officer in crime No.305/2021 of Shidlaghatta Rural Police has conducted the investigation in detail and has filed the charge sheet against the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA40F899 holding that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC Bus.
During the cross examination of PW.1 nothing worthwhile is elicited to show the absence of negligent on the part of the KSRTC Bus driver.
She has also examined Mr.Pramod - eye witness to the accident as PW.2.
He is the charge sheet witness No.2 as per Ex.P.7.
During his crossexamination, he has stated that he showed the accident spot to the police.
Nothing is brought out to disprove his version as eye witness to the accident.
Therefore, from the evidence of Pws.1 & 2 it can be gathered that there was negligence on the part of KSRTC Driver.
15. The PM report produced as per Ex.P.4 and Inquest mahazar produced as per Ex.P.5 clearly show that 'death SCCH-25 occurred due to injuries in RTA.
In support of their defence the respondent has got examined the Driver of the KSRTC bus as RW.1 but not produced any documents on his behalf.
During his cross examination he has admitted that Shidlaghatta - Vijayapura Road is around 30 feet wide, while driving he can seen the movements of about 150 feet in front of him.
The criminal case filed against him is still underway.
In DE proceedings against him his increment has been postponed and Rs.6,000/ fine is imposed.
He has denied that he had hit the deceased due to his rash and negligent driving when he was crossing the road and stated that he is not responsible for the death of the deceased.
Further denied the in the DE proceedings it is held that the mistake was from his side.
As per Ex.P.6sketch, the deceased was in the middle of the Road.

On an analysis of all the facts which have come before the court during the crossexamination of Pws.1 & 2 and RW.1 and on perusal of police documents, it is clear that the KSRTC vehicle and the deceased were both Kamalamma G.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164163181/
4 negligent.
However, the extent of negligence is different.

The SCCH-25 major part of the negligence in causing the accident lies with the Driver of the KSRTC bus, to whom this court is assigning 80%
of the negligence.
The deceased was also negligent in crossing the Road where there was a movement of vehicle and this court assigns 20% of the negligence on him.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was caused due to the negligence of Driver of KSRTC Bus and the deceased.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

16. Issue No. 3:
PW.1 has specifically spoken before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, they have lost the bread earner of their family and her loving husband.

She has further deposed that they have spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards conveyance,
transportation of dead body and for performing the funeral ceremonies.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation as per the following discussion.
SCCH-25 Monthly income 17.
According to the Petitioners, the deceased was doing Agriculture work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.
The Petitioner to prove the income of the deceased has not produced any documents such as Bank statement, RTCs etc., nor has she examined any witness.
Under such circumstances, this court has to consider the income of the deceased notionally for calculating the compensation.

18. The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.7404/2014 (MVD), by referring on the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Meena Pawaria and others Vs. Ashrafali and others (2021 SCC online sc 1083), Jakir Hussein Vs. Sabir (2015) 7 SCC 252, Smt. Neeta and others Vs. Divisional Manager, MSRTC Kolhapur (2015)3 scc 590, Kala Devi and Orthers Vs. Bhagwan Das Chouhan and Others (2015) 2 SCC 771, Sonobanu Nazirbhai Mirza Vs. Ahmadabad Municipal SCCH-25 Transport Service (2013) 16 SCC 719, Pushkar Mehra Vs. Brij Mohan Kushwaha and others (2015) 12 SCC 688, Govind Yadav Vs. The New India Insurance Company Limited and another (2011) 10 SCC 683 and Ningamma and another Vs. United India Insurance Company Limited (2009) 13 SCC 710 has held that "there is a continuous and consistent trend by the Apex Court that the Minimum Wages Act provide for a source by which the notional income of the deceased, who had no valid proof of income could be assessed.

It is pertinent to note that as per the Karnataka Government Notification of Minimum Wages for employment in Agriculture Work with effect from 01042021 to 3103 2022, the monthly income of a supervisor is Rs.11,473/ per month.

Therefore the notional income of the deceased can Kamalamma G.R vs K.S.R.T.C on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164163181/
5 be rounded off to Rs.11,500/ per month.

sentences.text: Age of the deceased 20.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced notarized copy of Aadhar card as per Ex.P.8.
As per Ex.P.8 the deceased was aged about 68 years.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
This shows that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased was 68 years.
Therefore, his age is considered as 68 years.
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE PROSPECTS:
As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation, appropriate SCCH-25 multiplier applicable to his age is 5.

sentences.text: In the instant case, the deceased has a wifepetitioner No.1 aged about 48 years and a major son - Petitioner No.2 aged about 26 years respectively.

PW.1 in her cross  examination admitted that the petitioner No.2 is working in a Private company, getting salary of Rs.15,000/ to Rs.16,000/.Therefore, it can be seen that petitioner No.2 was not depending on the income of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 wife is the sole dependent of the deceased.
However if the notional income is applied to the deceased (that of an Agriculturist), he would be earning around Rs.11,500/ per month.

21. As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged about above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

sentences.text: As mentioned above, since the deceased was above 60 years age slab, no future prospects is to be added to his monthly income.
As per the Sarala Verma case, if there is a sole dependent then SCCH-25 1/2 of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses, balance comes to Rs.5,750/.
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.3,45,000/ (Rs.5,750/ X 5 x 12) = Rs.3,45,000/).
ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018)

sentences.text: , the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".

22. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. SCCH-25 Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
23.

sentences.text: The Petitioner is the wife and as she has lost her husband and companion at the age of 48 years and she has to the live remaining part of her life without him, she is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/ under the head of loss of consortium.
Similarly, the petitioner No.2 is the son of the deceased, he has lost his loving, care taking father.
Therefore, he is also entitled to Rs.44,000/, in total Rs.88,000/ is awarded under the head of loss of consortium.

6 iii)
TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES:
PW.1/Petitioner has stated that she has spent Rs.1,00,000/ towards funeral expenses and obsequies etc..
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any bills pertaining to the above said expenses.
However, there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.
Therefore, in the interest of justice, SCCH-25 the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF ESTATE:
As mentioned above, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.11,500/ per month.
Out of this, he was spending 1/2 of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of estate.

As such, in total, the Petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.4,73,000/.
LIABILITY 24.
The Respondent has denied the negligence of the KSRTC Bus.
As already discussed this court has held that the KSRTC Driver is negligent to the extent of 80% and the deceased was negligent to the extent of 20%.
Therefore, the respondent being the owner is liable to pay 80% of the SCCH-25 compensation awarded by the court.

The petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.4,73,000/
out of which 20% shall be deducted due to contributory negligence of the deceased.
Though the Petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.30,00,000, Petitioners are entitled only for a sum of Rs.3,78,400/ (Rs.4,73,000/  Rs.94,600/) along with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 in the affirmative.
25. Issue No.4:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

SCCH-25  The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.3,78,400/ (Rupees Three Lakhs Seventy Eight Thousand and Four Hundred only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount from the Respondents.
The respondent liable to pay 80% of the total compensation awarded by this court to the petitioners.
The Respondent shall deposit the Award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgment.
On deposit of the award amount and interest, Rs.1,00,000/ shall be deposited in the name of the Petitioner No.1 in any N/S bank for a period of 3 years.

Out of the total SCCH-25 compensation Rs.44,000/ shall be released to the petitioner No.2 and the remaining amount shall be released to the petitioner No.1 by way of epayment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
